The Secret Life of Honeybees

By Jane Doe

Honeybees are among the most remarkable social insects on Earth, living in highly organized colonies consisting of thousands of individuals working together seamlessly.

Inside the hive, worker bees perform a variety of specialized roles that change as they age, from nursing newly hatched larvae to foraging for nectar and pollen across several square kilometers.

Recent studies suggest that colony communication involves not only the famous waggle dance, but also complex chemical signals that coordinate collective defense and temperature regulation.
